data.name: NoUsableForecast
data.value: No usable forecast, so no plan for today; the mode is charging on live surplus instead.

data.name: NoChargeableWindow
data.value: Today has no chargeable window: the sun never clears the charger's floor for long enough, or the home battery needs all of it. The car waits.

data.name: TodayGives
data.value: Today gives the car about {0}, in a window from {1:HH:mm} to {2:HH:mm}.

data.name: TargetMet
data.value: Target met: {0} of the {1} asked for has reached the car. The charger has been released.

data.name: Headline
data.comment: {0} is the energy still to deliver, {1} the departure time.

data.name: AlreadyInCar
data.value: {0} of the {1} asked for is already in the car.
data.comment: Appended to Headline, after a space.

data.name: MoreThanCanDeliver
data.value: {0} by {1} is more than the {2} left can deliver. Charging flat out from now, the car will have about {3} — {4} short.

data.name: LeavingInstead
data.value: Leaving at {0} instead would cover the full amount.
data.comment: Appended to MoreThanCanDeliver, after a space.

data.name: BatteryHeldOut
data.value: The home battery is held out of it while the grid tops the car up, so the pack is not emptied into a charge that was already going to fall short.

data.name: ForecastCoversAll
data.value: The forecast covers all of it: {0} from surplus {1}, and no grid import is planned at all.

data.name: BatteryKeepsPriority
data.value: The home battery keeps its priority throughout: the discharge hold arms whenever the car is drawing more than the roof is giving, so the pack never feeds it.

data.name: NoUsableForecastTargeted
data.value: There is no usable forecast for this window, so the plan assumes the grid will supply all of it. Any surplus that does appear is used first, and the plan is rebuilt on the next poll.

data.name: SunAndGrid
data.value: The sun should carry {0} of it {1}, and the grid the remaining {2}. Rather than charge flat out and finish early, the car is paced at about {3} across the window, so the charger draws close to what the roof is producing and buys only the shortfall.

data.name: UnusableSurplus
data.value: {0} of surplus is forecast for this window, but it never climbs past the charger's 6 A minimum, so the car cannot run on it unaided. It is still worth having: the charger is held at that minimum while the sun is up, the roof supplies what it has, and only the difference is bought — about {1} of grid on average.

data.name: AllFromGrid
data.value: No surplus at all is forecast before then, so the whole {0} still needed comes from the grid, paced at about {1} across the window. With no sun to wait for there is nothing to be gained by putting it off, and spreading it leaves room to recover if anything drops out.

data.name: HoldingNow
data.value: Everything below the rest level is in the car, and the last {0} is being held back until {1}. Nothing is wrong — the charger is idle on purpose, so the car reaches its target shortly before you leave rather than sitting full all night. Sun arriving before then is deliberately turned down; that is what this priority costs.

data.name: HoldingLater
data.value: The last {0} of it is held back until {1}, so the car finishes just before departure rather than hours early. Everything below the rest level is charged normally until then, on the sun wherever the sun is there.

data.name: ChargeModeTip
data.value: Starting any mode below puts the charger into Fast; Off stops the car, whichever mode was running. Nothing survives a restart — the service boots in Off and writes nothing until something here is pressed. Fast (no battery) and Targeted switch themselves off once the car finishes, Solar + grid once the day's useful sun is over, and the line above follows them without this page's help.

data.name: HoldTip
data.value: Common to every mode, which is why it sits above them: it stops the home battery serving household load, so the car charges from PV and grid while the battery can still charge from surplus. Shows the last command written successfully, not a device read-back — a failed write shows this switching back off on its own.

data.name: StartedAt
data.value: started from the Web UI at {0}

data.name: StoppedAt
data.value: stopped from the Web UI at {0}

data.name: SolarIntro
data.value: Charges from surplus the house isn’t using, once the home battery is full.

data.name: SolarTip
data.value: Charge from whatever the roof is making that the house is not already using. The home battery keeps first claim: this mode waits until the battery is full, then follows the surplus up and down, and pauses when there is not enough of it to hold the charger's minimum current.

data.name: StartSolarTip
data.value: Puts the charger into Fast and hands it to the surplus. Nothing else to set — the current is whatever the sun leaves over, decided again every poll.

data.name: SolarSurplusHint
data.value: PV left after household consumption — the smoothed 3-minute average this mode decides on. Blank while a mode that doesn't decide on surplus is driving.

data.name: BatterySocGateHint
data.value: The gate for this mode: the car gets nothing until the home battery is full.

data.name: EvPowerHint
data.value: What the charger reports the car actually drawing right now — not a setpoint.

data.name: TargetCurrentHint
data.value: The current this mode decided on this cycle, before it was written. Blank whenever it isn't charging.

data.name: SolarGridIntro
data.value: Follows the sun; the grid tops up to the charger’s minimum when surplus is small.

data.name: SolarGridTip
data.value: Charge from the sun, and let the grid help. While the surplus the house isn't using stays above your minimum, the car follows it; when that surplus is too small for the charger's minimum current on its own, the grid tops it up to that minimum, with the home battery held out of it. There is no full-battery gate. When the surplus drops below your minimum the car pauses — smoothed over a few minutes, so a passing cloud doesn't stop it — and once the forecast has no sun left today that clears the minimum, the mode switches itself off.

data.name: StartSolarGridTip
data.value: Puts the charger into Fast and hands it to the surplus. Ends by itself at the end of the day's useful sun, when the car stops drawing, or when it is unplugged.

data.name: MinSurplusTip
data.value: Below this the car pauses instead of taking grid. The most the grid ever adds is the charger's minimum power (about 4.1 kW at 6 A on three phases) less this figure; set it at or above that and the grid never helps at all. Also the line the rest of today's forecast has to clear. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: SolarGridLowTariffHint
data.value: In high tariff the car waits, sun or not, and charges as above once low tariff starts. The mode still ends with the day's useful sun, so a low tariff that starts after dark charges nothing here. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: SunUntilHint
data.value: When the forecast says the surplus stops clearing your minimum today — when this mode will switch itself off if the live surplus agrees. Only shown while this mode is driving.

data.name: GridPowerTopUpHint
data.value: Positive while importing. While the grid is topping up a small surplus, this is roughly that top-up.

data.name: UntilFullTip
data.value: Keeps one session going over several days, for a car left at home over a weekend or a week: one sunny afternoon rarely fills it, three usually do. By day nothing changes. Where the mode would end for the day, it stands the charger down for the night instead and starts again on the next day's sun. It ends when the car is full, is unplugged, or you press Off. A session running with it on is resumed after a restart.

data.name: UntilFullDay
data.value: Running until full: day {0} of this session.

data.name: NoTariffYet
data.value: Set up a tariff in {0} first; until then this has nothing to wait for.

data.name: LowTariffIgnoredNote
data.value: Set, but ignored: there is no tariff to wait for, so it charges whatever the hour.

data.name: ForecastedIntro
data.value: Charges from surplus, guided by the forecast so the home battery still fills by evening.

data.name: ForecastedTip
data.value: Charge from surplus like {0}, but with the fixed battery-full gate replaced by the Solcast forecast: the plan decides how much of today's remaining sun the car may have, so the home battery still reaches 100% by the evening deadline. The midday plateau goes to the car, the shoulders stay with the house and the battery.

data.name: StartForecastedTip
data.value: Falls back to plain surplus behaviour whenever no usable forecast is available, rather than refusing to charge.

data.name: WhereChargeStopsTip
data.value: This mode takes no amount: it charges the car from whatever surplus the forecast says the home battery will not need, until the car's own charge limit stops it. To keep the car below full, set that limit in the car. To {0} for an amount by a time, use {1}: when the forecast covers it in time, it charges from the sun alone, and it buys grid only if the sun falls short.

data.name: MinBatterySocTip
data.value: The lowest the home battery may go while it helps charge the car. When it gets there the car pauses until the battery has recovered by the resume margin below. The plan may keep a higher floor when the forecast says the battery needs it to be full by the plan's deadline. Shared with the Targeted mode, so changing it here changes it there too. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: ResumeMarginTip
data.value: How far above the floor the battery must recover before a paused session restarts. Raise it if the car starts and stops repeatedly on a marginal day. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: PlanOnlyWhileForecasted
data.value: The day plan is only shown while {0} is the active charge mode. Current mode: {1}.

data.name: PlanStateHint
data.value: Why the plan decided what it decided -- the same line the log carries.

data.name: ChargeWindowHint
data.value: The next stretch of today forecast to clear the charger's minimum power for long enough to be worth starting. 'none' when today offers no such window.

data.name: EvBudgetHint
data.value: How much of today's remaining sun the car may have, restricted to periods where the surplus actually clears the charger's minimum power.

data.name: ProjectedShortfallHint
data.value: How far today's forecast falls short of the house plus a full home battery. Above zero, the evening 100% is at risk. The car is not in this sum — it only ever gets what is left over.

data.name: SurplusSpillHint
data.value: Remaining surplus the home battery has no room for — what is still coming less what it can absorb. At 100% it is all of it, and every watt leaves the house unless the car takes it, which is what lets the battery lend against a much thinner surplus.

data.name: LoanHeadroomHint
data.value: How much the pack may lend right now: the room between its SOC and the floor, capped by the spill. Zero when SOC sits on the floor, or when every remaining watt has a home in the pack.

data.name: RequiredFloorHint
data.value: The SOC the battery must not fall below right now for the sun still to come to return it to 100% by the deadline. Battery SOC dropping to this line is what pauses the car.

data.name: ForecastRemainingHint
data.value: Forecast PV still to come today, at the configured confidence band and already scaled by forecast accuracy.

data.name: TomorrowForecastHint
data.value: Tomorrow's forecast production. Purely informational: context for whether a shortfall today is worth waiting out.

data.name: ForecastAccuracyHint
data.value: Actual production against forecast so far today. 100% is on the nose; the rest of the day's forecast is scaled by this, and a sustained large miss makes the plan untrusted.

data.name: LoanedTodayHint
data.value: Energy the home battery has lent the car today so a surplus below the charger's floor could still reach it. Resets at local midnight.

data.name: IntoCarSincePlugged
data.value: {0} into the car since it was plugged in.

data.name: FastIntro
data.value: As fast as the installation allows, with the home battery kept out — expect grid import.

data.name: FastTip
data.value: Charge as fast as the installation allows and keep the home battery out of it. The setpoint is pinned at the configured maximum whatever the sun is doing: PV covers what it can and the grid covers the rest, so expect to import. The discharge hold is armed when the charge starts and released when it ends — you can switch it off in between if you would rather the battery helped.

data.name: EnergyNeededTip
data.value: Measured at the charger, from the moment you press the button.

data.name: ReadyByTip
data.value: No time set: the charge starts straight away. With a time, the charge is held back and starts as late as it can while still finishing before you go — so a car asked to go above 80% spends minutes there rather than the whole night, which is what actually ages the pack. It still charges flat out when it runs; only the start moves. To remove a time you have set, open the calendar and press its Clear button.

data.name: FastLowTariffHint
data.value: In high tariff the car waits, and it charges flat out once low tariff starts. The charger starts a car on its own when it is plugged in, so one plugged in during high tariff draws for a moment until the next poll stops it. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: FastEvPowerHint
data.value: What the charger reports the car actually drawing right now — not a setpoint. This is what falls away when the car decides it is full.

data.name: FastEvCurrentHint
data.value: Charging current derived from the charger's measured power: what the car really takes, which can be below the maximum if the car itself limits it.

data.name: ActiveCurrentHint
data.value: The charger's setpoint read back from the hardware: what it was actually left at.

data.name: FastGridPowerHint
data.value: Positive while importing from the grid, negative while exporting. In this mode it is the price of the speed.

data.name: DeliveredHint
data.value: Energy delivered against the amount asked for, metered at the charger from the moment this charge was started. The mode stops itself when it gets there.

data.name: BasisEnergyHint
data.value: The charge stops when that much has been delivered, or when the car stops first — whichever comes first.

data.name: BasisSocHint
data.value: Converted to kilowatt-hours once, when you press the button. A later reading from the car does not move a charge that is already part delivered.

data.name: BasisFullHint
data.value: The car decides: the charge runs until it reaches its own charge limit and stops drawing.

data.name: BasisFullNoSocHint
data.value: The car decides: the charge runs until it reaches its own charge limit and stops drawing. A battery target needs the car's capacity in Vehicle:BatteryCapacityKWh and a reading from the car.

data.name: EndsFullHint
data.value: Ends itself: when the car stops drawing because it has reached its own charge limit, the setpoint drops to the pause current and the mode returns to Off, which releases the hold.

data.name: EndsAmountHint
data.value: Ends itself: at the amount above, or when the car stops drawing first. Either way the setpoint drops to the pause current and the mode returns to Off, which releases the hold.

data.name: NoUsableSoc
data.value: No usable SOC reading to measure the gap from.

data.name: AlreadyAt
data.value: The car is already at {0} — nothing to do.

data.name: SocConversion
data.value: From {0} now, that is about {1} at the charger: {2} usable, {3} of what the charger meters reaching the cells.

data.name: FastDelivered
data.value: The {0} asked for has been delivered; the charge is stopping.

data.name: FastProgress
data.value: {0} of {1} is in the car; {2} to go before this stops itself.

data.name: PowerMaximum
data.value: {0} (the installation's maximum — the car has not drawn yet)

data.name: NotEnoughTime
data.value: Not enough time: about {0} of this will not fit before {1:HH:mm}. Charging flat out from now at {2}.

data.name: WaitingUntil
data.value: Waiting until {0:HH:mm}, then charging flat out: {1} at {2} takes about {3}, and the car is wanted by {4:HH:mm}.

data.name: ChargingToBeReady
data.value: Charging flat out to be ready by {0:HH:mm}: {1} to go at {2}.

data.name: TargetedPlanStateHint
data.value: Complete: the target is met. Solar: the forecast covers it with no import at all. SolarPlusGrid: the sun carries what it can and the grid paces the rest. Maximum: there is not enough time, so everything available is taken.

data.name: StillNeededHint
data.value: The request less what the charger has measurably delivered since it was activated.

data.name: DeliveredSoFarHint
data.value: Measured at the charger, so a car that limits itself to less than we asked for simply gets a longer grid block on the next poll.

data.name: ForecastSurplusHint
data.value: All the surplus this window is forecast to hold, after the house and the home battery's booking — whether or not the car can charge on it unaided.

data.name: FromSunHint
data.value: The part of the surplus above that the car can actually run on alone. Zero does not mean no sun: it means no half-hour clears the charger's 6 A minimum, which is why the grid block is placed over the sunniest hours rather than after them.

data.name: FromGridHint
data.value: What the sun cannot cover. Rebuilt every poll, so a better day than forecast shrinks this before the rest of it is bought.

data.name: ChargePaceHint
data.value: The average the grid must sustain to keep the promise: what is still needed, less the sun forecast to reach the car, over the time left. The charger runs at this plus whatever the roof is giving, so sun above it is free and lowers it for later. Zero means the forecast covers the target outright.

data.name: ChargingFromHint
data.value: When the first grid-funded charging starts. The charge is spread across the window rather than run flat out, because the charger can only use the sun that shines while it runs.

data.name: ExpectedByDepartureHint
data.value: What will actually reach the car. Below what was asked for only when there is not enough time left.

data.name: ShortfallHint
data.value: How far the plan falls short of the request. Anything above zero means the departure is too soon for the amount asked for.

data.name: HeldBackHint
data.value: The last stretch of the target, scheduled to land just before departure instead of whenever the sun offers it — so the car does not sit at a high state of charge all night. Everything below it is charged normally.

data.name: ReleasedAtHint
data.value: When the held stretch starts. Worked out from the charger's maximum power plus a slack margin; if the car takes it more slowly than that, the pace rises on the next poll and the shortfall figure reports it if even that will not do it.

data.name: BatterySocFloorHint
data.value: Below this, the sun goes to the home battery and the car gets only what the deadline needs, from the grid. Never lower than your Minimum battery SOC; higher when the forecast leaves the battery too little sun to refill.

data.name: ReadyByHint
data.value: The finish line the plan works to: your departure less the safety margin.

data.name: ReportedByCar
data.comment: {0} is how old the reading is ("12 min").

data.name: ReportedByCarVia
data.value: Reported by the car {0} ago via {1}.
data.comment: {1} is the name of the feed the reading came from.

data.name: JustInTimeExtra
data.comment: The pacing option with what it costs: {0} is the extra grid energy, signed ("+2.1 kWh").

data.name: TargetedIntro
data.value: Say how much and by when; forecast sun goes first, the grid covers the rest as late as possible.

data.name: TargetedTip
data.value: Say how much the car needs and when it has to be there, then look at the plan before it starts. The plan takes every kilowatt-hour of forecast surplus the home battery has not already claimed, and buys the rest from the grid as late as it can and still finish in time.

data.name: StaleCheck
data.value: Stale — older than {0}, so the feed may have died. Check the figures against the car before planning from them.

data.name: CarBatteryHint
data.value: The car's own state of charge, as its cloud integration last reported it. Not the home battery.

data.name: RangeHint
data.value: What the car reckons is left in it, off its own recent consumption. Display only — no plan reads it — but it is the figure that answers whether the target you are about to set is enough for the trip.

data.name: PluggedInHint
data.value: What the charger sees at the socket, and what the car says about its own. The charger is the faster of the two and the one the controller acts on; the car can lag it by hours.

data.name: CarChargeStateHint
data.value: What the car says it is doing: Idle, Charging, Complete, or Unknown when it doesn't report.

data.name: AimingAtTip
data.value: Either way the promise is metered in kilowatt-hours at the charger. A battery target is converted once, when you start it — a later reading from the car does not move a target that is already part delivered.

data.name: EnergyNeededStartTip
data.value: Measured at the charger, from the moment you press Start.

data.name: PacingTip
data.value: Both meet the departure. {0} paces the charge across the window and takes every watt of sun above that pace, so the target is usually met well before you leave. {1} delivers everything up to the rest level the same way, then holds the last stretch back so the car is not sitting full overnight — which costs grid, because the sun is turned down while it waits.

data.name: SunOnlyTip
data.value: Nothing is bought from the grid. Whatever the sun can't deliver by the departure is reported as shortfall, not imported — the preview shows how much before you start. A cloud the 3-minute average hasn't caught up with can still draw a little from the grid while the car runs at its minimum, so expect close to none rather than exactly none.

data.name: SunOnlyNoJustInTime
data.value: Just in time is off while this is ticked: holding the last stretch back with no grid to make up a cloudy hour can only lose sun.

data.name: ReadyByTargetTip
data.value: Charging finishes a few minutes before this, so the car is ready rather than still drawing. At most {0} ahead.

data.name: MinBatterySocTargetedTip
data.value: Below this level the home battery comes first: the sun charges it, and the car gets only what it needs to be ready on time, from the grid. At or above it, the car also takes the solar surplus. The home battery never charges the car in this mode. On a poor-sun day the plan may keep a higher floor so the battery can still refill. Shared with the Forecasted mode, so changing it here changes it there too. Doesn't persist across restarts.

data.name: PreviewTip
data.value: Preview writes to nothing — it is the same planner the poll loop runs, asked what would happen if you started now. The request does not survive a restart of the service: if it restarts overnight the car stops charging, and nothing will have told you.

data.name: IfYouStartNow
data.value: The plan, if you start now

data.name: NoPollForPlan
data.value: No poll has completed yet, so there is nothing to build a plan from — no battery SOC, no house load, no forecast anchored to an instant. You can still start the target and the plan will appear on the first poll.

data.name: PlanOnlyWhileTargeted
data.value: The plan is only shown while {0} is the active charge mode. Current mode: {1}.

data.name: AskingSoc
data.value: Charging to {0}, from the {1} the car last reported: {2} at the charger, charge losses included.

data.name: NoSocForRest
data.value: No usable SOC reading to measure the rest point from.

data.name: AlreadyAboveRest
data.value: The car is already at {0}, at or above the {1} rest level, so the whole charge is the held stretch and none of it will start until the release time.

data.name: FinishesBelowRest
data.value: This target finishes at about {0}, at or below the {1} rest level, so there is nothing above it to hold and the charge runs as it would under Cheapest.

data.name: RestExplained
data.value: The car charges on the sun up to {0} whenever the sun is there, then waits. The last {1} — about {2} to {3} — is scheduled to land just before you leave.

data.name: HoldCostsNothing
data.value: Holding the last stretch costs nothing here — the forecast has no sun to give it up.

data.name: HoldCost
data.value: Just in time buys about {0} more from the grid than charging as cheaply as possible would, because the sun is turned down while the tail waits. That is the trade: the car sits at {1} overnight instead of at its target.
